m-intro.supports: Discrete models, proof, and computer-science applications.

m-propositions.supports: Statements, truth values, predicates, and counterexamples.

m-implication.supports: Direct and contrapositive implication proofs; both directions of an equivalence.

m-cases.supports: Proof by cases, contradiction, and clear mathematical argument.

m-wop.supports: Least counterexamples, well ordering, and prime-factor existence.

m-connectives.supports: Negation, conjunction, inclusive/exclusive disjunction, implication, and truth tables.

m-equivalence.locator: §§3.3–3.4; §3.4.2, p. 59, equations (3.7) and (3.12) for commutativity and double negation
m-equivalence.supports: Validity, equivalent formulas, Boolean laws, and justified rewrites.

m-quantifiers.supports: Predicate domains, quantification, order, and negation.

m-sequences.supports: Indexed sequences and recursive integer functions.

m-functions.supports: Functions, composition, partial/total conventions, arrow diagrams, and finite cardinality. This notebook uses total functions unless stated otherwise.

m-relations.supports: Relations as ordered pairs and arrow representations.

m-induction.supports: Base case, induction hypothesis, implication step, and invalid induction.

m-strong.supports: Strong induction, recursive splitting, and equivalence with ordinary induction.

m-divisibility.supports: Divisibility, greatest common divisors, primes, and factorization.

m-digraph.supports: Directed degrees, walks, and adjacency matrices.

m-composition.supports: Relational composition, reachability, and positive/reflexive walk closures.

m-orders.supports: DAG scheduling, partial orders, cover representations, and total orders.

m-classes.supports: Equivalence classes, partitions, and relational properties.

m-graph.supports: Simple graphs, adjacency, degree sums, and common graph families.

m-walks.supports: Paths, components, and Euler/Hamiltonian walks. Terminology conventions are stated in the lesson.

m-trees.supports: Trees, forests, spanning trees, and equivalent tree properties.

m-sums.supports: Finite geometric and power sums, telescoping, and bounds.

m-products.supports: Products, factorial estimates, and sums with two indices.

m-asymptotic.supports: Eventual growth bounds, little-o, theta, and common asymptotic pitfalls.

m-counting.supports: Sum/product/division rules, ordered choices, combinations, and repetition.

m-pigeonhole.supports: Pigeonhole arguments and finite mapping constraints.

m-pie.supports: Inclusion–exclusion, binomial identities, and counting in two ways.

m-recursive.supports: Unfolding, Hanoi, merge sort, and recurrence verification.

m-linear-rec.supports: Characteristic roots, repeated roots, and nonhomogeneous linear recurrences.

m-divide-rec.supports: Recursion levels, divide-and-conquer recurrences, and bounds.

m-subset-bits.supports: Representing subsets by fixed-position bit sequences, with 1 for membership and 0 for exclusion, and counting the subsets of a finite set. The bit-mask table is an original example of this correspondence.

p-sets.supports: Set definitions, power sets, Cartesian products, indexed families, and Venn reasoning.

p-logic.supports: Connectives, conditional forms, truth tables, and logical equivalence.

p-quantifiers.supports: Quantifiers, English translation, negation, and logical inference.

p-direct.supports: Definitions, parity, divisibility, direct proof, and cases.

p-contra.supports: Contraposition, congruence examples, and mathematical writing.

p-contradiction.supports: Contradiction proofs, irrationality, and combining proof techniques.

p-setproof.supports: Element proofs of membership and inclusion, equality by both inclusions, and De Morgan identities. Hammack uses an overbar for complement where this notebook uses a superscript c.

p-disproof.supports: Genuine counterexamples and refuting existential assertions.

p-relations.supports: Relation properties, equivalence classes, and partitions.

p-functions.supports: Total functions, injectivity, surjectivity, inverses, images, and preimages.

p-multisets.supports: Stars and bars, division/pigeonhole principles, and combinatorial proof.

i-vectors.supports: Vector coordinates, addition, scaling, and linear combinations.

i-subspaces.supports: Subspaces, column spaces, and null spaces.

i-basis.locator: §§2.7.1–2.7.3: basis and dimension definitions; column-space and null-space bases; Basis Theorem and proof
i-basis.supports: Bases and dimension; extracting or extending a basis; selecting original pivot columns and homogeneous solution vectors. The equal-size basis theorem is stated; the lesson supplies its own exchange argument.

i-coordinates.supports: Unique coordinates relative to a basis.

i-rank.supports: Rank, nullity, and the rank theorem.

i-reduction.supports: Row operations, pivots, and echelon forms.

i-parameters.supports: Free variables and parametric solution sets.

i-transform.supports: Linearity and recovering a matrix from basis images.

i-multiply.supports: Composition, matrix products, transpose, and algebraic laws.

i-diagonal.supports: Eigenbases, repeated action, and failures of diagonalization.

i-dot.supports: Dot product, norm, angles, and orthogonality.

i-projection.locator: §§6.3.1–6.3.2: Orthogonal decomposition; Closest vector and distance; line-projection recipe and proof; projection properties

i-orthonormal.locator: §§6.4.1–6.4.2: orthogonal independence, Projection Formula, normalization, and Gram–Schmidt theorem/proof including zero remainders
i-orthonormal.supports: Orthogonal and orthonormal bases, projection sums, and Gram–Schmidt with span preservation and redundant-vector removal. The source orthogonalizes before normalizing; the lesson normalizes each retained direction.

i-least.locator: §§6.5.1–6.5.2: normal-equation theorem, uniqueness criteria, and Best-fit line
i-least.supports: Normal equations, orthogonal residuals, unique fitted outputs, rank-dependent parameter uniqueness, and least-squares fitting of vertical discrepancies. The source orders slope before intercept; the lesson orders intercept before slope and defines residual as observations minus fitted output.

ml-intro.supports: Motivation for mathematical data models and linear algebra.

ml-affine.supports: Linear maps, kernel/image, change of basis, and affine spaces.

ml-svd.supports: Full and reduced SVD, rectangular dimensions, singular directions, and numerical cautions.

ml-models.locator: §8.1, printed pp. 251–258 (PDF pp. 257–264), especially §8.1.4: fitting training observations versus predicting unseen data
ml-models.supports: Models, data, and the limits of mathematical interpretation.

d-intro.supports: Scope and examples of discrete mathematics.

alg-search.locator: Lectures 13–14: BFS; DFS and topological sorting
alg-search.supports: Adjacency lists, breadth/depth-first traversals, complexity, and scheduling.

alg-cost.locator: Lecture 2: Models of Computation; Recitation 1: asymptotic complexity
alg-cost.supports: Cost models, input size, asymptotic analysis, and worst-case interpretation.

tex-supported.supports: Math commands, grouping, scripts, spacing, and matrix/aligned/cases environments. Foundations supports a curated subset; editor controls are app-specific.

tex-delimiters.locator: Auto-render extension: delimiters and ignored text
tex-delimiters.supports: Inline/display math delimiters; Foundations uses its own parser and deliberately supports single-dollar inline math.

js-every.supports: Finite-array predicate checks and empty-array behavior.

js-some.supports: Finite-array predicate checks and empty-array behavior.

js-floor.supports: Rounding direction and the distinction between integer truncation and floor/ceiling.

js-ceil.supports: Rounding direction and the distinction between integer truncation and floor/ceiling.

js-trunc.supports: Rounding direction and the distinction between integer truncation and floor/ceiling.

history-logic.supports: Historical distinction between term logic and Stoic propositional logic.

history-graph.locator: E53: archive summary and English translation

svd-approx.locator: Low-rank approximation, Solution, and Relation to SVD
svd-approx.supports: Frobenius-optimal truncated SVD and residual error from discarded singular values.

numerical-rank.supports: Singular-value thresholds and the distinction between exact and numerical rank.

numerical-ls.locator: Linear Least Squares (LLS) Problems: xGELS paragraph, rank-deficient driver paragraph, and Table 2.3
numerical-ls.supports: QR/SVD methods, full-rank and rank-deficient least-squares problems.

alg-asymptotic.locator: Recitation 1, pp. 1–4: asymptotic complexity and binary search
alg-asymptotic.supports: Upper, lower, and tight bounds; logarithmic growth and binary-search recurrences.

i-determinant-area.locator: §4.3.2: Determinants and volumes theorem, transpose observation, Area example, and Signed volumes remark
i-determinant-area.supports: Absolute determinant as parallelogram area and determinant sign as orientation in the plane. The source first uses rows, then explicitly extends the volume statement to columns; the lesson uses columns.

i-existence-uniqueness.locator: §§3.2.1–3.2.3: one-to-one and onto matrix-transformation theorems; square-matrix comparison
i-existence-uniqueness.supports: Independent columns give at most one input per output; full row rank reaches every output. These are separate conditions for rectangular matrices and coincide for square matrices.

strang-row-space.locator: §3.5, printed pp. 182, 184–185 (PDF pp. 2, 4–5): nonzero echelon rows; The Four Subspaces for A, items 1–2
strang-row-space.supports: Nonzero echelon rows form a row-space basis; reversible row operations preserve row span; row rank and column rank equal the pivot count. Row reduction need not preserve the column space.

numerical-solve.locator: Linear Equations: simple-driver description and paragraph immediately before Table 2.2
numerical-solve.supports: Linear-system drivers factor the coefficient matrix and solve without explicitly forming its inverse; explicit inversion is generally unnecessary for solving systems.

lapack-qr.locator: QR Factorization: reduced factorization A=Q1 R and full-column-rank least-squares application
lapack-qr.supports: Orthonormal columns and upper-triangular reconstruction coefficients in reduced QR, matrix dimensions, and triangular least-squares solving. The lesson names the rectangular factor Q; this source names it Q1. LAPACK implementation is not claimed to use classroom Gram–Schmidt.

fnc-normal-stability.locator: The normal equations — Conditioning and stability, equations (65)–(66)
fnc-normal-stability.supports: Sensitivity of least-squares coefficients to perturbations and possible numerical instability from forming normal equations: in the 2-norm, the condition number of A transpose A squares that of A.

review-witness.locator: Quantifiers and Equality, The Existential Quantifier
review-witness.supports: A witness is a domain value satisfying an existential condition. Supports original definition recall prompts and generated integer examples, not copied source exercises. Integer examples independently checked by substitution.

review-logic-statements.locator: §1.1, Definition 1.1.5 and Atomic and Molecular Statements
review-logic-statements.supports: Statements with definite truth values, including false or unchecked claims; contrast with questions, commands, and unassigned free variables. Supports original retrieval prompts and examples, not copied textbook exercises.

review-logic-basics.supports: Propositions, truth values, negation, conjunction, disjunction, exclusive OR, implication, and biconditional names and truth conditions. Original prompts follow this curriculum's notation and examples.

review-logic-conditionals.supports: Antecedent and consequent roles; the sole false implication case; converse, inverse, and contrapositive; refutation by a case meeting the antecedent and violating the consequent. Prompts preserve curriculum terminology, which does not introduce hypothesis as an antecedent synonym.

review-logic-conditional-language.supports: Necessary and sufficient conditions; direction of if and only if; biconditionals assert both implication directions. Supports original wording and notation variants, not copied examples.

review-logic-equivalence.supports: Complete truth tables, independent truth assignments, equivalence by matching all rows, contraposition, De Morgan's laws, and implication rewrites. Original compound formulas and counterassignments were independently checked over every truth assignment.

review-logic-negation.supports: Negation of implication as a true antecedent with a false consequent; De Morgan transformations; strict versus non-strict inequality negation. Original boundary examples were independently checked below, at, and above each boundary.

review-logic-classification.supports: Precise distinction among tautology, contradiction, and contingency according to all possible truth assignments. Original retrieval items distinguish all, some, and no true rows.

review-logic-arguments.supports: Arguments, premises, conclusions, and validity as true premises forcing a true conclusion. Validity is distinct from the actual truth of the premises. Supports original definition and distinction prompts.

review-logic-counterassignments.supports: An assignment with every premise true and conclusion false refutes validity. Original counterassignment construction variants and feedback were checked independently by truth-table evaluation; the examples are not copied from the source.

review-logic-models.locator: Propositional Theories, numbered slide 9 (PDF page 8); Horn Bounds, numbered slide 11 (PDF page 10)
review-logic-models.supports: In propositional logic a model is an actual truth assignment under which the formula or theory is true. Supports the model terminology distinction; MIT references separately support satisfiability and unsatisfiability.

review-predicate-meaning.supports: Predicate inputs and substitution into a truth-valued condition. Supports original definition and distinction prompts, not copied exercises.

review-quantifier-meaning.supports: Universal and existential terminology and truth conditions, explicit domains, finite-domain interpretations, and witness membership. Original numeric examples independently verified.

review-domain-order.supports: Domains, mixed-quantifier order, dependent versus fixed witnesses, validity and countermodels. Supports original interpretations and constructions; examples independently checked.

review-variable-scope.supports: Scope, free and bound occurrences, formulas with no free variables, and safe renaming without capture. The curriculum uses explicit parentheses rather than relying on scope conventions; it calls formulas with no free variables closed.

review-quantifier-negation.supports: Negation of universal, existential, nested, and conditional quantified statements while preserving domains and variable order. Original comparison-boundary variants independently checked.

review-quantifier-counterexamples.supports: Domain-valid counterexamples to universal and conditional claims; refuting existence requires excluding all candidates. Original boundary and numeric examples independently verified.

review-unique-existence.supports: Exactly-one quantification as existence plus at-most-one uniqueness, including the zero-solution distinction. Matches the curriculum's explicit separation of existence and uniqueness.

review-empty-domain.supports: Universal truth and existential falsity for an explicitly empty domain; nonempty-domain requirement for inferring existence from a universal claim. The source normally assumes nonempty domains but explains the empty-domain contrast; the curriculum permits emptiness only when stated.

review-quantifier-distribution.locator: §§8.2–8.3, universal conjunction and existential disjunction proofs
review-quantifier-distribution.supports: Universal conjunction and existential disjunction distribution. The original separate-witness countermodel was exhaustively checked over its two-element domain.

mml-transpose.supports: Transpose shape and the row/column exchange defining each transposed entry; original numerical examples are independently calculated.

m-recursive-data.locator: §7.1, Recursive Definitions and Structural Induction (printed pp.217–220)
m-recursive-data.supports: Base objects, recursive constructors, nested pairs, and additive occurrence counts.

os1-calculus-preface.supports: The relationships among change, accumulation, single-variable calculus, and the later multivariable sequence. App study instructions describe this curriculum rather than a textbook claim.

os1-2-2.supports: Infinite one-sided limits and vertical asymptotes.

os1-2-5.supports: Epsilon–delta definition, quantifier order, and linear-function proofs.

os1-3-8.supports: Implicit differentiation, chain factors on dependent variables, tangent slopes.

os1-3-9.supports: Combining exponential/logarithm derivatives with earlier rules.

os1-4-2.supports: Differentials, relative error and limits of linear approximation.

os1-4-4.supports: MVT consequences, constant derivatives and monotonicity.

os1-4-5.locator: §4.5 derivatives and the shape of a graph
os1-4-5.supports: First/second derivative tests and inconclusive zero second derivatives.

os1-4-8.supports: Infinite-over-infinite limits, products, differences and variable powers.

os1-4-7.supports: Cost/revenue optimization, distance objectives and interpretation.

os1-5-4.locator: §5.4 Integration Formulas and the Net Change Theorem
os1-5-4.supports: Accumulating a derivative and displacement versus distance.

os1-4-10.supports: Antiderivative families on intervals, basic formulas, and initial conditions.

os1-5-3.supports: Differentiation of accumulation functions and evaluation using antiderivatives.

os1-5-5.supports: Reverse chain rule and change of bounds for definite integrals.

os2-3-1.supports: Product-rule derivation, definite integration by parts, and repeated applications.

os2-3-4.supports: Polynomial division, distinct and repeated linear factors, and irreducible quadratic factors.

os2-3-2.supports: Odd powers, even-power identities, and tangent/secant patterns.

os2-3-3.supports: Radical substitutions and restrictions ensuring the correct square-root sign.

os2-2-1.supports: Vertical and horizontal slices, curve intersections, and compound regions.

os2-2-5.supports: Mass from linear density, work, and lifting variable contributions.

os2-3-6.supports: Midpoint, trapezoidal, and Simpson formulas, derivative error bounds, and absolute/relative error.

os2-3-7.supports: Infinite intervals, unbounded integrands, separate limits, and comparison.

os2-5-1.supports: Sequence limits, squeeze arguments, subsequences, and bounded monotone convergence.

os3-4-5.supports: The Chain Rule: definitions, hypotheses, methods, and interpretation supporting the original explanations and calculations.

os3-4-7.supports: Maxima/Minima Problems: definitions, hypotheses, methods, and interpretation supporting the original explanations and calculations.

os3-4-8.supports: Lagrange Multipliers: definitions, hypotheses, methods, and interpretation supporting the original explanations and calculations.

ps-os-4-4.supports: Geometric memorylessness and the identical variance of trials and failures conventions; formulas independently reconciled.

ps-os-stat-1-1.locator: §1.1 Definitions of Statistics, Probability, and Key Terms
ps-os-stat-1-1.supports: Populations, samples, parameters, statistics, and descriptive versus inferential questions.

ps-os-stat-1-2.locator: §1.2 Data, Sampling, and Variation in Data and Sampling
ps-os-stat-1-2.supports: Data types, probability sampling designs, convenience sampling, missing data, and sampling variation.

ps-os-stat-2-5.locator: §2.5 Measures of the Center of the Data
ps-os-stat-2-5.supports: Means, medians, modes, weighted frequency calculations, and grouped-data limitations.

ps-os-stat-2-7.locator: §2.7 Measures of the Spread of the Data
ps-os-stat-2-7.supports: Sample variance, standard deviation, centered sums, and changes of units.

ps-os-stat-1-4.supports: Observational studies, explanatory/response variables, random assignment, masking, and responsible reporting.

ps-pn-7-1-1.supports: Sample-mean moments, weak law of large numbers, and finite-variance deviation proof.

ps-pn-7-1-2.supports: Iid finite-variance CLT, standardized CDF convergence, approximation examples, and continuity correction.

ps-pn-5-3-2.supports: Independent normal sums are normal; marginal normality alone is insufficient without joint assumptions.

ps-pn-6-2-2.supports: Nonnegative-variable bounds, centered second-moment bounds, and indicator-variable union bounds supporting the original guarantees and calculations.

ps-pn-8-2-1.supports: Bias, variance, mean squared error, consistency, and finite-variance sample-mean error bounds.

ps-pn-8-2-3.supports: Likelihoods from joint mass/density, independent products, logarithms, and elementary parameter maximization.

ps-os-8-1.locator: §8.1 A Single Population Mean using the Normal Distribution
ps-os-8-1.supports: Repeated-sampling confidence, known-standard-deviation mean intervals, normal quantiles, margin of error and sample-size planning; original calculations use explicitly stated assumptions.

ps-os-8-2.locator: §8.2 A Single Population Mean using the Student t Distribution
ps-os-8-2.supports: Estimated standard errors, degrees of freedom, Student t quantiles, and mean intervals under the stated sampling model.

ps-os-8-3.supports: Large-sample normal intervals for proportions, plug-in standard errors and sample-size planning; the lesson explicitly limits the approximation near boundaries.

ps-os-9-1.supports: Population hypotheses, one- and two-sided alternatives, and reject versus fail-to-reject decisions.

ps-os-9-4.locator: §9.4 Rare Events, the Sample, Decision and Conclusion
ps-os-9-4.supports: Tail probabilities under a null model, significance comparisons, and conclusions supported by the test.

ps-os-9-3.locator: §9.3 Probability Distribution Needed for Hypothesis Testing
ps-os-9-3.supports: Normal and Student reference models, proportion standard errors under the null, and sampling assumptions; the authored lesson explicitly uses a more conservative expected-count screen of at least ten.

ps-os-9-2.locator: §9.2 Outcomes and the Type I and Type II Errors
ps-os-9-2.supports: Testing errors, significance and power, with original worked examples distinguishing effect sizes and decisions.

ps-pn-9-1.supports: Priors, observation likelihoods and normalized posterior distributions for parameter uncertainty.

ps-pn-9-2-beta.locator: §9.2 End of Chapter Problems: beta distribution and beta-binomial conjugacy problems
ps-pn-9-2-beta.supports: Beta density and moments, binomial updating, and posterior normalization; the lesson uses independently calculated original integer-parameter examples.

ps-regression-os-12-3.supports: Least-squares slope and intercept, residuals, squared errors, residual plots, and restrictions on extrapolation; examples are original.

ps-regression-mml-9-1-2.supports: Independent Gaussian observation models and the equivalence between maximum likelihood and least squares for fixed common error variance.

ps-regression-islr-3-1.supports: Residual variance, coefficient standard errors, t tests and confidence intervals with n−2 degrees of freedom under the normal-error model.

ps-regression-psu-3-2-3.locator: Lesson 3 §§3.2–3.3: mean-response confidence interval and new-response prediction interval
ps-regression-psu-3-2-3.supports: Exact simple-linear-regression mean and prediction standard errors, t multipliers, and the extra variance of a future observation.

ps-regression-islr-3-3.locator: §3.3.3 Potential Problems, printed pp.92–101 / PDF pp.101–110
ps-regression-islr-3-3.supports: Nonlinearity, correlated errors, nonconstant variance, outliers and high leverage; numerical intervals rely on the specified model.

ps-assessment-islr-5-2.locator: §5.2 The Bootstrap, printed pp.187–190 / PDF pp.195–198
ps-assessment-islr-5-2.supports: Sampling observations with replacement, preserving predictor-response pairs, repeated bootstrap estimates, and their sample standard deviation as an estimated standard error.

ps-assessment-islr-5-1.supports: Validation splits, held-out squared prediction error, k-fold cross-validation, and the distinction between training fit and model assessment.

ps-assessment-mml-8-2-6.locator: §8.2 Empirical Risk Minimization and §8.6 Model Selection, printed pp.259–266 and 283–288 / PDF pp.265–272 and 289–294
ps-assessment-mml-8-2-6.supports: Population versus empirical loss, held-out assessment, selection, overfitting and differing costs; examples compute finite expected losses independently.

ps-assessment-islr-4-4.supports: Confusion matrices, sensitivity/recall, specificity, precision, false-positive rates, and effects of classification thresholds.

probability-statistics-katex.locator: Supported Functions: Accents, Greek Letters, Logic and Set Theory, Operators, Fractions, Big Operators, and Style, Color, Size, and Font (Font)
probability-statistics-katex.supports: Probability notation, accents, bold Latin and Greek vector symbols, relations, and operator constructions in the authored optional typing help.

review-df-set-basics.supports: Membership, empty sets, cardinality, subsets, power sets and Cartesian products; supports original terminology retrieval.

review-df-set-operations.supports: Membership definitions of union, intersection, difference and complement relative to a universe. Original finite examples are computed from these definitions; notation uses setminus and superscript c.

review-df-partition.supports: Nonempty, pairwise disjoint blocks covering a set; original partition and disjointness terminology.

review-df-relations.supports: Relations, reflexivity, symmetry, transitivity, equivalence relations and equivalence classes; original finite relation instances.

review-df-function-types.supports: Total functions, domain, codomain and range; original terminology and domain/codomain examples.

review-df-function-properties.supports: Injective, surjective and bijective functions; dependence on domain/codomain. Original finite and square-function classification examples.

review-df-function-inverse.supports: Composition order and types, inverse functions and preimages; original terminology retrieval.

review-df-direct.supports: Direct proof starts with the hypothesis and derives the conclusion from established facts and definitions.

review-df-contrapositive.supports: Contrapositive proof assumes the negated conclusion and establishes the negated hypothesis.

review-df-contradiction.supports: Contradiction proofs negate the whole target; conditional and quantified proof setups. Original assumption-selection tasks follow these rules.

review-df-orders.supports: Antisymmetry and reflexive partial orders. The curriculum calls the book’s weak partial order a partial order; loops are allowed. Original finite classification instances.

review-df-proper-subset.supports: Proper inclusion is subset inclusion together with inequality; the curriculum writes subsetneq to make its convention explicit.

review-df-sequence-growth.supports: Recursive rules, initial values, arithmetic sequences and geometric sequences. Original terminology retrieval follows the taught distinction between starting values and continuation rules.

review-df-sum-notation.locator: §2.2, summation notation preceding the proof of Theorem 2.2.1, p. 31
review-df-sum-notation.supports: Summation indices enumerate the included terms and empty sums equal zero; original endpoint, singleton and empty-index calculations.

review-df-sequence-definitions.supports: Recurrence relations determine later terms from earlier terms; initial conditions supply starting values. Original retrieval distinguishes the rule from the data.

review-la-vectors.locator: §§2.1.1–2.1.3: vectors, scalar multiplication, and linear combinations
review-la-vectors.supports: Coordinate-vector and scalar terminology; sum-of-scaled-vectors definition; original recognition examples.

review-la-dot.locator: §§6.1.1–6.1.2: dot product, length, and orthogonal vectors
review-la-dot.supports: Dot-product terminology, zero dot products, zero-vector edge case, and independently checked finite examples.

review-la-matrix.supports: Matrix-product dimensions and composition order; original short dimension probes.

review-la-transpose.supports: Transpose as interchange of rows and columns.

review-la-systems.supports: Consistency means at least one simultaneous solution.

review-la-free.supports: Nonpivot variables parameterize a consistent system; a free variable does not itself establish consistency.

review-la-homogeneous.supports: A zero right-hand side defines a homogeneous system and guarantees a zero solution.

review-la-span.supports: Span is the set of all real linear combinations of the supplied vectors.

review-la-independence.locator: §§2.5.1–2.5.2: definition, zero-vector fact, and redundancy criterion
review-la-independence.supports: Linear independence, nontrivial dependence, and the distinction between pairwise nonparallel vectors and an independent list.

review-la-spaces.supports: Input null spaces versus reachable column spaces; terminology and ambient spaces.

review-la-basis.supports: Independent spanning lists and dimension; original finite examples.

review-la-coordinates.supports: Coordinates relative to an ordered basis are the unique reconstruction coefficients.

review-la-rank.supports: Rank is column-space dimension, nullity is null-space dimension, and their sum is the number of input columns.

review-la-inverse.locator: §3.5.1: inverse definition; §3.5.2: two-dimensional determinant and inverse criterion
review-la-inverse.supports: Two-sided inverse and two-dimensional determinant terminology.

review-la-linear-map.locator: §3.3.1: linearity definition, zero-image fact, and nonlinear examples
review-la-linear-map.supports: Linearity preserves addition and scaling; taking zero to zero is necessary but insufficient.

review-la-kernel-image.locator: §2.7.3, Definition 2.23 and Null Space and Column Space remark, printed pp. 58–59 (PDF pp. 64–65)
review-la-kernel-image.supports: Kernel and image terminology; input versus output spaces.

review-la-projection.locator: §6.3.1: Orthogonal decomposition theorem, closest-vector definition, and line-projection recipe
review-la-projection.supports: Projection and residual terminology; both subspace membership and perpendicular residual are required.

review-la-least.locator: §6.5.1: least-squares definition, normal-equation theorem, and uniqueness theorem
review-la-least.supports: Least-squares terminology; orthogonal residuals; a unique fitted output with nonunique coefficients. Original transfer problems use the curriculum residual b−Ax convention.

review-la-eigen.locator: §§5.1.1–5.1.2: eigenvalue/eigenvector definitions, zero-vector note, and eigenspace
review-la-eigen.supports: Eigenvalues are scalar multipliers and eigenvectors must be nonzero.

review-la-svd.supports: Full SVD terminology, nonnegative singular values, rectangular factors and rank. The curriculum lists min(m,n) singular values including zeros.

review-la-fit-limits.locator: §8.1.4, printed pp. 257–258 (PDF pp. 263–264): learning, prediction, and evaluation
review-la-fit-limits.supports: A fit to observed data does not establish accuracy on unseen inputs. Original contrasting functions illustrate the distinction without asserting that this book contains the examples.

review-dm-induction.supports: Base case, induction hypothesis, general implication step; original role distinctions.

review-dm-invariant.locator: §6.2, Definition 6.2.5 and Invariant Principle, printed pp. 177–178
review-dm-invariant.supports: Initialization and preservation of loop invariants; the curriculum uses loop invariant for the resulting property at loop boundaries.

review-dm-strong.supports: Strong induction permits all earlier cases in the stated domain.

review-dm-well-ordering.supports: Nonempty nonnegative-integer sets have a least element; smallest-counterexample reasoning. The positive-real halving counterexample is original and independently checked.

review-dm-counting.supports: Product/sum rules, permutations, subset counting and uniform overcount correction. Original small counts independently enumerated; no source claim for the specific examples.

review-dm-pigeonhole.supports: More objects than boxes forces at least one repeated assignment.

review-dm-inclusion-exclusion.supports: Two-set inclusion–exclusion and the double-counted intersection.

review-dm-recurrence.supports: Recurrence evaluation, order, homogeneous/inhomogeneous terms, characteristic equation and polynomial. Original recurrence values and polynomial factorizations independently checked; source uses boundary conditions where curriculum says initial conditions.

review-dm-graphs.supports: Vertices, simple undirected edges, adjacency and degree. Unlike this source, the curriculum permits empty graphs; these review prompts do not change that convention.

review-dm-routes.locator: §2.1, vocabulary entries Walk, Path, Cycle, Connected; compared with MIT MCS §§12.7–12.8
review-dm-routes.supports: Walk/trail/path distinction and connectivity. Levin permits a path to repeat its starting vertex at the end; these original review prompts explicitly retain the curriculum/MIT convention: paths have no repeated vertices, cycles are separate. Graph cases independently checked.

review-dm-trees.locator: §2.2, Definition 2.2.1, tree edge count and Rooted Trees subsection
review-dm-trees.supports: Trees/forests, n−1 tree edges, designated root and child relationships. Rooted leaf here means no children, including a singleton root; this differs from an unrooted degree-one leaf.

review-dm-dag.supports: DAG terminology and topological ordering. The original two-prerequisite example has two valid orders.

review-dm-asymptotics.locator: Recitation 1, Asymptotic Complexity and Asymptotic Drowning, pp. 1–3
review-dm-asymptotics.supports: O/Omega/Theta directions, dominant terms and exact-count versus growth distinctions. Uses nonnegative functions on positive integer sizes as taught. Original examples independently verified.

review-dm-cost.locator: Measuring Runtime, paragraph defining worst-case T(N) as maximum over inputs of size N
review-dm-cost.supports: Worst-case takes the maximum over inputs of each fixed size; best-case takes the minimum. Original terminology retrieval and contrasting Big O distractor.

review-dm-search.locator: Lecture 13, p. 5, Analysis: sum of adjacency-list lengths, undirected 2|E| and vertex overhead
review-dm-search.supports: Summed neighbor-entry work plus vertex overhead. Original tree/complete-graph exact counts follow independently from the explicitly stated unit-cost model.

review-dm-big-o.supports: Fixed constant and threshold preceding all later inputs; polynomial dominant terms and distinction between upper and tight bounds. Curriculum uses eventually nonnegative functions on positive integers.

review-dm-growth-hierarchy.supports: Polynomial, logarithmic and exponential growth hierarchy, especially each fixed polynomial power being little-o of an exponential with fixed base greater than one. Original recognition variants retain the curriculum’s positive-integer input convention.
